findings.summary: The command-word contract excludes quoted executable tokens in command position, so the promised lint can be bypassed by a pwsh call-operator invocation.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261125-2207-b40-i156-mixed-os-pwsh.loop-brief.md:210-217 defines a command word as outside quotes while naming '&' as a command boundary. In pwsh, `& 'grep' -n ok a.txt` and `& "/usr/bin/GREP.exe" ok` invoke the listed executable, but neither quoted token can match under that definition. The text nevertheless says every gate call to a listed command is refused at lines 219-226.
findings.fix: Specify command-position tokens separately from argument strings: a wholly quoted token is an executable name when it is the command word, including immediately after `&`, but stays data in argument position. Add refused literals for `& 'grep'` and `& "/usr/bin/GREP.exe"`, while retaining `Select-String -Pattern 'grep'` as accepted.

findings.summary: The proposed task gates explicitly run tests that the same tasks are to add, making the judge task-reachable.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261125-2207-b40-i156-mixed-os-pwsh.loop-brief.md:423-439 gates tasks 1-3 on "tests it adds" and task 4 on the structural tests it changes. This contradicts docs/domain/domain-model.md:210-212, P-8, and plugin/skills/gate-review/SKILL.md:100-103, which classify a gate that runs a task's own test as `task-reach`.
findings.fix: State that the added tests are exercised by the `go` check, and have the planner put independent oracle tests and fixture commands in each task's gate folder. Each task gate must exercise the named CLI/driver/skill behaviour without running a test file the work session can edit.

decisions: Any two distinct declared platforms, including linux+macos, require pwsh.
The shared key is `platforms`, with only `linux`, `macos`, and `windows` as values.
`platforms` is shared-only; in a mixed team, `shell` is shared-only and an override is an error even when its value is pwsh.
Portability is enforced by a deterministic driver lint, reinforced by plan and gate-review guidance, using the fixed command list.
The default-shell doctor finding is a warning rather than a problem for compatibility.
Plans do not record `platforms`; accepted plans retain their recorded shell and only the next plan is linted.
Shared-only errors apply to every command that reads config.
`vloop task verify` replacements and existing plans are not linted.
Gate-script scanning is limited to `.ps1` files under the gate folder.
